# Handover for unit 1.1

## What landed

`8d96e35` — `givenSettings` now marks the harness, model and effort as given
only when they came from a flag or the plan's front matter. A value from
`.ploopy.toml` still prefills the board, but is no longer locked. The new board
test `TestChangingTheAgentResetsAFileModelAndEffort` shows that changing the
agent resets a file model and effort to the new harness's defaults.

## Landmark drift

None. `cmd/ploopy/settings.go` and `cmd/ploopy/board.go` were as the work order
described.

## Deviations from the work order

None. The defect was the single assignment that set `g.harness`, `g.model` and
`g.effort` from non-empty values; the booleans are now set in the flag and plan
branches instead, and the assignment is gone.

## What the next session must know

- `fill` already preserved a file prefill through `g.prefilled(...)`, so removing
  the "non-empty means given" rule does not lose the file value on first show.
- `normalize` in `board.go` resets model and effort when `!given.model` /
  `!given.effort` and the agent changed, which is what the new test exercises.
- `TestChangingTheAgentKeepsAGivenModelOrEffort` (flags) still passes, as does
  the whole `cmd/ploopy` suite.

## Open problems

None.

# Handover for unit 1.2

## What landed

`a787a0b` — a `[run] effort` from `.ploopy.toml` is validated against the
harness the run will use even when `[run] agent` is absent: the last run's
harness when ploopy can still drive it, else the default. The error names
`[run] effort`. An `[review] triage_effort` from the file that the settled
triage harness does not offer now names `[review] triage_effort` instead of
`the triage effort for ...`.

## Landmark drift

None. `givenSettings`, `fill` and `chooseSettings` in
`cmd/ploopy/settings.go`, and `chooseTriageWithSources` / `validateTriage` in
`cmd/ploopy/triage.go`, are where the work order placed them. Unit 1.1 had
already landed its `given` change as described.

## Deviations from the work order

- The run check stayed in `givenSettings` rather than moving after `fill` in
  `chooseSettings`: `chooseSettings` returns to `unattended` before `fill` when
  not interactive, so post-`fill` validation could not be reached in tests.
  `givenSettings` now calls a small `settledHarness` helper that applies
  `fill`'s own precedence (last run, else default) purely for the check; it
  does not mutate the settings, so `fill` still settles the board.
- The triage check is an adjacent guard before `validateTriage`
  (`chooseTriageWithSources`), using the `sources` map to tell a file value
  from a flag or last-triage value. `validateTriage` itself is unchanged, so
  flag and last-triage errors keep their existing text.

## What the next session must know

- `TestAFileEffortIsCheckedAgainstTheHarnessTheRunSettlesOn` covers both the
  last-run and default cases: claude does not offer `max`.
- `TestAFileTriageEffortIsCheckedAgainstTheTriageHarness` covers default
  claude (`max` invalid) and a last triage on opencode (`medium` invalid).
- `settledHarness` guards a nil `cmd.Context()`; tests build commands without
  `SetContext`.

## Open problems

None.

1.3.handover:
# Handover for unit 1.3

## What landed

`5bdc990` — a field's "from .ploopy.toml" source is now recomputed on every
board redraw: `given` records the file's value beside the label, and the
Triage column's `sources` map records the file's values instead of a fixed
label. A source appears only while the current field value still equals the
file's value; changing it, or a normalize/normalizeTriage replacement, clears
it; setting it back restores it.

## Landmark drift

None. `given` and its `fromFile`/`prefilled` are in `cmd/ploopy/settings.go`,
`chooseTriageWithSources` in `cmd/ploopy/triage.go`, and the column builders
in `cmd/ploopy/board.go`, where the work order placed them.

## Deviations from the work order

- `given.fileValues` is a second map beside the existing `prefills` label map,
  so `fill`'s presence checks and existing source-label tests keep working.
  The board uses a new `source(key, current)` while `prefilled(key)` still
  reports whether a file value exists.
- `chooseTriageWithSources`' `sources` map changed from key -> label to key ->
  the file's value; the board derives the label, and the pre-existing effort
  validation now tests presence of that entry. Its only consumers are the
  board and tests.

## What the next session must know

- `TestAFileSourceLeavesWhenTheRunFieldChanges` covers a `[run]` Bedrock
  field (peak); `TestAFileSourceLeavesWhenTheRunColumnFieldChanges` covers the
  Run column (finish); `TestAFileSourceLeavesWhenTheAutomationFieldChanges`
  covers follow-up; `TestAFileSourceLeavesWhenTheTriageAgentChanges` covers
  the triage agent plus normalized model and effort.
- One existing assertion in `TestTheReviewTableBeatsTheLastTriageAndFlagsBeatTheReviewTable`
  now expects the source map's values to be the file's values, not the label.
- `fromFile` now takes the value as well as the key. Secondary and rescue are
  recorded after resolution so `none` maps to the board's empty value.
- The adjust board has no file prefills, so it still shows no source labels.

## Open problems

None.

# Handover for unit 1.4

## What landed

`b7b320d` — the `loop.Options` literal in `runOnce` moved into
`runOptions` (`cmd/ploopy/run.go`), taking the plan, config, skills, flags and
the settled `chosenRun`. A new test,
`TestTheChosenRescueReachesTheLoopOptions` in `cmd/ploopy/settings_file_test.go`,
calls it with a `chosenRun` holding a rescue and finds `Options.Rescue` set to
that agent, and with no rescue finds it nil. Deleting `Rescue: pick.rescue`
from `runOptions` makes the test fail (verified, then restored).

## Landmark drift

None. The literal was still at `cmd/ploopy/run.go:319`, and `Loop.steer` still
reads `Options.Rescue` only for a nil `Options.Steering` as the work order
describes.

## Deviations from the work order

- The whole literal moved into `runOptions`, not just the rescue assignment.
  The unit's start hint allowed this; it is the simplest way for the test to
  build the real options rather than a copy of one field.
- The function takes the resolved verify and test commands as arguments, so
  `runOnce` keeps its command/flag fallback and `--test` validation before the
  call.

## What the next session must know

- `runOptions` is a pure constructor: later in `runOnce`, `opts` is still
  mutated for dry run, fresh-worktree setup, branch, lending and steering.
  Anything added to the literal belongs in `runOptions`; anything computed
  from the checkout after it stays in `runOnce`.
- `TestTheChosenRescueReachesTheLoopOptions` uses `boardEnv` and a zero
  `runFlags`, so it checks only the rescue field, not the flag plumbing. The
  existing file/flag/last-run rescue test still covers the plumbing into
  `chosenRun.rescue`.
- Both required checks are green: `go build -o /dev/null ./... && go vet ./...
  && test -z "$(gofmt -l .)"` and `go test ./...`.

## Open problems

None.

2.1.handover:
# Handover for unit 2.1

## What landed

`a4297a1` — `followsUp` now requires `loop.Result.Status == "done"` and refuses a
run whose `planRun.limited` is set. `planRun` carries `limited`, set from
`--until`/`--units` in `runOnce`; `runChainedPlan` clears both flags, so a
chained plan is never limited. The start line passes the same limit to
`followUpSuffix`, which now takes a `limited` argument and stays silent for it.
The README `follow_up` bullet and the *Automation* text of
`skills/ploopy/SKILL.md` say `--until`/`--units` and a failed run end the chain.

Tests added in `cmd/ploopy/run_chain_test.go`: a finished one-unit plan run with
`--follow-up --until 1.1` and with `--units 1` starts no review and writes no
review file; a run whose state commit fails after the last unit landed starts no
review and exits with the loop's "Resume with" error; `followUpSuffix` covers an
ordinary plan, a review, a fix plan, limited runs and follow-up off. Both
behaviour tests were confirmed to fail with the old `followsUp` and pass after
the change.

## Landmark drift

None. `followsUp` and `followUpSuffix` were at the cited places in
`cmd/ploopy/run.go`; the `--until`/`--units` returns in `internal/loop/loop.go`
are as described.

## Deviations from the work order

- `limited` is derived from the run flags in `runOnce` rather than stored on
  `Loop.Options`. The loop already exposes the flags, but the chain decision is
  `cmd/ploopy`'s and the flags are what the author typed.
- The failure test faults the state commit with an `index.lock` created after
  the unit's own commit, rather than a git-hook or reload failure. The on-disk
  state file then says the last unit landed while `loop.Run` returns `failed`,
  which is exactly the cited case.

## What the next session must know

- `planRun.limited` is recomputed from `runFlags` at `runOnce`'s return. If a
  later unit changes how `--until`/`--units` are cleared for chained plans,
  keep `runChainedPlan`'s `next.from, next.until, next.units = "", "", 0`.
- `--until`/`--units` are also on the `review` command's run flags; a review
  started with them will now not chain to its fix plan, per F-D1.
- `followUpSuffix` has three call sites' worth of contract in its test; it is
  still used only by the start line.

## Open problems

None.

commits: 922bc47f4ff4871601e7a2e10ee7247bcc45d1b6 Say whether the chain runs the fix plan next
2.2.handover:
# Handover for unit 2.2

## What landed

`922bc47` — the run no longer tells the author to start a fix plan it is about
to start, and a chained fix plan no longer advertises a follow-up.

- `runOnce` registers `FollowUp: nil` in the live settings for a plan where
  `review.IsFix(p.Path)`, so `ploopy status`/`ploopy adjust` during a chained
  fix plan cannot say "then review and fix". The start line still uses
  `followUpSuffix`, which already said nothing for a fix plan.
- `reviewOutcome` takes a `runsNext` bool. `runOnce` decides it with the same
  `chainedFixPlan` the chain uses, so a finished review under `--follow-up`
  says "the fix plan is X: running it next" and a review that ends keeps
  "run it with `ploopy run --plan X`".

Tests in `cmd/ploopy/review_chain_test.go`: one reads `control.List` while the
first fix-plan session runs and rejects "review and fix" in `Wanted.Describe`;
one captures the run's stdout with and without follow-up and checks which
sentence reviewOutcome printed. Both were confirmed to fail at `c7d8462` (the
fix-plan status there says "no end action · then review and fix") and pass here.

## Landmark drift

None. `announce`, `reviewOutcome` and `chainedFixPlan` are where the order
placed them.

## Deviations from the work order

- The `runsNext` decision reuses `chainedFixPlan` with a temporary `planRun`
  built from what `runOnce` already knows, rather than duplicating
  `followsUp`'s conditions. That keeps the message and the actual chain
  decision from drifting apart.
- `limited` is now computed once, before the announce, and reused by the start
  line and the returned `planRun`.

## What the next session must know

- `reviewOutcome(root, p, runsNext)` is called only from `runOnce`. A future
  caller that prints the manual line must pass `false`.
- `runOnce` now sets `FollowUp` nil for fix plans in the announced settings
  only; `pick.followUp` itself is unchanged, and `followUpSuffix` still reads
  it. `chainedPlan` still guards fix plans with `review.IsFix` even though
  `followsUp` is now false for them.
- An author can still `ploopy adjust --follow-up` during a fix plan: the
  setting will be laid over the nil base and `Describe` would then show
  "then review and fix". No chain results, because `chainedPlan` refuses a fix
  plan anyway. This is outside 2.2's stated contract but worth knowing if a
  later unit tightens the adjust board.

## Open problems

None.
